cases.name: High-cardinality categorical null handling
cases.input: A categorical column named 'product_category' has 8% nulls in the training set. How should I handle them?
expected_behaviors: Recommends filling with a sentinel string (e.g. 'UNKNOWN') rather than dropping rows
Explains that dropping rows in a sparse dataset loses training signal
Suggests adding a binary has_product_category flag if the null itself may be predictive
Does NOT recommend mode imputation for high-cardinality categoricals
should_not: Recommend dropping rows with null product_category
Recommend mode imputation without caveats for high-cardinality columns

cases.name: High cardinality entity ID encoding
cases.input: An entity ID column has over 4000 unique values. What encoding strategy should I use?
expected_behaviors: Recommends target encoding or frequency/count encoding
Warns that target encoding must be computed inside CV folds to prevent leakage
States that one-hot encoding is impractical at 4000+ cardinality
Mentions that LightGBM and CatBoost can handle high-cardinality categoricals natively as category dtype
should_not: Recommend one-hot encoding for 4000+ unique values
Apply target encoding across the full dataset before splitting (leakage)

cases.name: Deduplication on composite key
cases.input: I suspect there are duplicate rows in the training dataset. How should I deduplicate?
expected_behaviors: Identifies the natural composite key for the dataset (e.g. entity_id + date + context_id)
Keeps the most recent row if duplicates exist with different feature values
Verifies duplicate count before and after deduplication
Does not deduplicate on a single column if the same entity can appear at multiple contexts or dates
should_not: Deduplicate on a single ID column without considering the full natural key
Drop all columns and deduplicate on the full row without explaining the key
